title: How do you swap digits to land in a range?
description: Tanvi's parcel number is changed by swapping two digits so it lands between two limits and then above a target. The video picks each swap by checking the front digits.
teaching_notes: One idea: choose the digit that goes into the leftmost place by looking at the range, then check. Watch for a swap that overshoots the upper limit.

source: Let Us Do 5 (b), digit swap in 10,593
video_script.why: The child can swap digits but has not yet chosen a swap to land inside a range or past a target.
video_script.substitution: For a range, keep the front digit and choose a thousands digit that stays inside; for a target, bring a big enough digit to the front.
video_script.anchor: Tanvi's parcel number at the post office
video_script.wrong_answer: swap the zero and the nine
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu swaps the zero and the nine to make the thousands digit as big as possible and gets 19,503. That is above fifteen thousand, so it is outside the range.
video_script.payoff_line: the number becomes thirteen thousand, five hundred and ninety

final_answer.spoken: thirteen thousand five hundred and ninety, and fifty thousand one hundred and ninety-three

maths_rules: parcel 10,593 has digits 1, 0, 5, 9, 3: ten thousands 1, thousands 0
slip: swap 0 and 9 gives 19,503; 19,503 > 15,000, so it is outside the range
(i) between 11,000 and 15,000: the thousands digit must be 1 to 4 with 1 in front; swap 0 and 3 gives 13,590; 11,000 < 13,590 < 15,000
(ii) more than 35,000: the front digit must be 3 or more; swap 1 and 5 gives 50,193; 50,193 > 35,000
video_script.design: Exercise: two swaps with two targets. Hint: look at the front digits. The parcel with digit boxes stays on the stage.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='parcel'/>Tanvi's parcel at the post office is numbered ten thousand, five hundred and ninety-three.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Swap two digits so that the number is between eleven thousand and fifteen thousand. Then swap two digits so that it is more than thirty-five thousand.

<bookmark mark='second'/>For the second part, the front digit must be three or more. Try again with this.

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>Swap the zero and the nine for the first part. It makes the thousands digit as big as possible.
<bookmark mark='big'/>That gives nineteen thousand, five hundred and three.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>It is more than fifteen thousand, so it is too big.

narration: <bookmark mark='pick'/>For the first part, look for a digit from one to four to put in the thousands place.
<bookmark mark='three'/>The three fits. Swap the zero and the three.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>The number becomes thirteen thousand, five hundred and ninety, which is between eleven thousand and fifteen thousand.

<bookmark mark='five'/>The five fits. Swap the one and the five.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>The number becomes fifty thousand, one hundred and ninety-three, which is more than thirty-five thousand.

<bookmark mark='rule'/>Compare the front digit first, then the thousands digit.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Is your first number between eleven thousand and fifteen thousand, and your second more than thirty-five thousand?
